The process

Four steps to renew on time

Do the continuing education first. Your provider reports the hours to CTEC, and CTEC will not let you renew until those hours appear on your record.

01
Complete 20 hours of continuing education
Course provider

Use a CTEC-approved provider. The 20 hours are split across federal tax law, federal tax updates, ethics and California tax law. Reporting speed varies by provider, which matters if you are close to the deadline.

02
Renew your PTIN with the IRS
IRS

PTINs expire on December 31 each year. Renewal opens in the autumn on the IRS website.

03
Keep your $5,000 bond current
Surety company

Your surety bond must be valid for the full registration period. Check the expiry date and renew it before it lapses.

04
Renew with CTEC and pay the fee
CTEC

Sign in to your CTEC account, confirm your education has been reported, update your details, and pay the renewal fee before October 31.

Questions

Common questions

More answers on the FAQs page.

?
What if my provider has not reported my hours?

Contact the provider first. Most report within a few business days; near the deadline, ask for confirmation before you attempt to renew.

?
Can I carry over extra hours to next year?

No. Continuing education hours count for the renewal period in which they were completed.

?
I missed October 31. What now?

Renew during the late window, November 1 through January 15, with the late fee. After January 15 the registration lapses.

?
Do I need the same provider every year?

No. You can change providers each year; only CTEC approval matters.

?
My registration already lapsed.

Complete a 60-hour qualifying education course and register again as a new preparer, including the background check.
